questions.title: Rational function features
solution: Vertical asymptote: x=2. Horizontal asymptote: y=2. The x-intercept is (-5/2,0), and the y-intercept is (0,-5/2). Since (2x+5)/(x-2)=2+9/(x-2), the function never equals 2, so the range is R excluding {2}.

stem: A particle has velocity v=1/(t+2)+e^(-t), t>=0. Initially its displacement from O is zero.
questions.title: Kinematics and integration
solution: An antiderivative is ln(t+2)-e^(-t)+C. Using s(0)=0 gives 0=ln2-1+C, so C=1-ln2. Hence s(t)=ln((t+2)/2)+1-e^(-t).

stem: Events A and B satisfy P(A intersect B')=1/4, P(A' intersect B)=x and P(A union B)=3/4.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Express P(A intersect B), P(A) and P(B) in terms of x.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Given that A and B are independent, find x and all four regions of the probability diagram.

questions.title: Probability and independence
solution: The union contains the three disjoint regions, so P(A intersect B)=3/4-1/4-x=1/2-x. Hence P(A)=3/4-x and P(B)=1/2. Independence gives 1/2-x=(3/4-x)(1/2), so x=1/4. Therefore A only=1/4, B only=1/4, intersection=1/4 and neither=1/4.

questions.title: Composite functions and transformations
solution: f(x)=1+4/(x-3), so the asymptotes are x=3 and y=1. Intercepts are (-1,0) and (0,-1/3). Since g(f(x))=f(x)-2, the graph translates down 2 units. g o f=(7-x)/(x-3), domain R excluding {3}, range R excluding {-1}.

stem: A cubic f has stationary points at x=-1 and x=3, and f(0)=4, f(-1)=9.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Show that f'(x)=3a(x+1)(x-3) for a constant a.

questions.title: Cubic functions and stationary points
solution: Write f'(x)=3a(x+1)(x-3). Integrating gives f(x)=ax^3-3ax^2-9ax+d. Since f(0)=4, d=4. Also f(-1)=5a+4=9, so a=1 and f=x^3-3x^2-9x+4. f''=6x-6: f''(-1)<0 gives a local maximum; f''(3)>0 gives a local minimum. At x=0 the slope is -9 and the point is (0,4), so y=-9x+4.

stem: For 0<theta<pi/2, a force is modelled by F(theta)=120/(sin(theta)+2cos(theta)).

parts.label: b
parts.html: Find the exact angle at which F is minimized.

parts.label: d
parts.html: justify that the value is a minimum.

questions.title: Trigonometric optimization
solution: Let D=sin(theta)+2cos(theta). Then F'=-120(cos(theta)-2sin(theta))/D^2. Thus F'=0 when tan(theta)=1/2. Also D=sqrt(5)sin(theta+arctan2), whose maximum is sqrt(5), so F is minimized there. The exact minimum is 120/sqrt(5)=24sqrt(5). The derivative changes from negative to positive, or equivalently D has a maximum, confirming a minimum.
